top_categories.workout_context: Nordsjørittet's mixed terrain forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 54 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Nordsjørittet's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
Nordsjørittet's mixed terrain rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At Nordsjørittet, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
54 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
At Nordsjørittet, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Nordsjørittet. Train it until it feels boring.
2-minute all-out efforts on mixed terrain. Closing gaps, responding to attacks, sprinting for position. Train the burn.
Long rides with hard efforts mixed in. Simulates what Nordsjørittet's mixed terrain actually does to you.
Varied gradients on mixed terrain demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 40–60g carbs/hour for Nordsjørittet’s 54 miles. Front-load calories in the first half. One bottle per hour minimum, more in heat.
race_overlay.altitude: Moderate altitude at Nordsjørittet. Arrive 2–3 days early. Reduce intensity expectations by 5–10%. Hydrate aggressively.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at Nordsjørittet requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Road Specific, Race Simulation, and VO2max to prepare you for 54 miles of mixed terrain in Egersund to Sandnes, Norway.
